concerns.summary: The plan has the Skills write warnings such as "never `git add -A`" and "never suggest `--env stage` or `--env prod`", and has adops-share describe a Pull Request workflow that runs `run --all`, but the new tests fail any Skill whose text contains those same strings, so the correctly written Skills would fail their own checks.
concerns.cheapestFix: Decide on one rule before writing: either the forbidden-pattern tests skip lines that are clearly prohibitions or explanations, or the Skills phrase those warnings without quoting the banned command. Add a self-test that shows a correctly written warning line passes.

concerns.summary: The confirmed quality bar asks for one test that replays the Git steps of both adops-share and adops-breaking-change, but the planned test only replays the Breaking Change record commit and checks the share Skill by searching its text for a few command strings, so it would still pass if adops-share put the steps in the wrong order or added the wrong paths.
concerns.cheapestFix: Make the replay also do adops-share's own steps (branch first, add only the named paths pipelines/, dbt/ and adops.yaml, commit, push), or say clearly in the plan that share is checked by text only and get the user to agree.

concerns.summary: The last phase says the replay test catches a wrong command order, but the test runs its own hard-coded commands instead of reading them from the Skill files, so that claim is not true and the text check only confirms each command appears somewhere in the file.
concerns.cheapestFix: Either have the test check that the commands appear in the Skill text in the same order the test runs them, or remove the claim so nobody relies on a guarantee the test does not give.

concerns.summary: adops-promote is told to drop "the Branch Environment the user ran from their laptop" while the Pull Request workflow drops "the Server's copy", but a Branch Environment is one set of schemas in the shared stage Warehouse, so both may be the same schemas and the Skill's explanation could be wrong.
concerns.cheapestFix: Before the Skill is written, check whether a laptop branch run and a Server branch run use the same schemas. Then have adops-promote describe what actually happens, for example that dropping it by hand only speeds up a cleanup the workflow does anyway.

concerns.summary: The success criteria call for one E2E test, but the plan puts the Git replay in the unit test folder with a prepared record, which is a reasonable choice to save CI time but differs from what was written.
concerns.cheapestFix: Have the user confirm that a unit-level replay using a prepared record satisfies criterion 5, or reword criterion 5 to match.
